title: Fort Ville-Marie
geometryBasis: Archaeological excavations at 214 Place D’Youville and the 2015 sidewalk trench establish the historic site. Pointe-à-Callière describes about 2,500 square metres in a rectangular plan oriented roughly parallel to the Saint Lawrence, with four timber bastions. The geographic control comes from the current excavated parcel and current nearby river-edge axis. The footprint is a constrained reconstruction.
sectionBasis: The museum and archaeology literature confirm the palisade trench, possible guardhouse, stone foundations for metallurgical work and 1658 timber-lined well. The McGill catalogue’s written description of Bourdon’s early manuscript lists the chapel and magazine. Morin’s later drawing provides general placement and roof cues, with the excavated timber enclosure taking precedence. Heights and complete building placement are estimates.

dimensions.innerRanges: Interpretation based on the archive plans and written archaeological evidence.

limitations: The four-corner outline and overall area follow the museum’s modern archaeological findings. Specific corners, gate, heights, internal areas and the Saint-Pierre river shoreline are interpretations.

Bourdon documents an early scheme of uncertain date. Morin’s 1884 illustration is retrospective. Only Morin’s illustration provides visual clues. The McGill text reports architectural functions from the Bourdon manuscript.

The ancient occupation level was approximately two metres below the present street in the excavated area. The model shows the historical fabric in a dated geographic preview using today’s unmodified terrain datum. No modern shoreline or archaeological terrain was sculpted.
